papers.title_en: Belief-Conditioned Multi-Agent Actor Critic for Decentralized LLM Collaboration
papers.authors: Tianle Chen, Shuo Liu, Christopher Amato
papers.evidence: 面向去中心化大模型协作的多智能体演员评论家及Minecraft实验
papers.tldr: LLM多智能体协作常依赖预设流程，去中心化场景下通信受限，且需从交流痕迹推断信息，效率与扩展性不足。BCMAAC用信念条件化多智能体actor-critic，维护上下文信念并用于训练。在Minecraft、网页搜索和工具使用任务上，它优于朴素actor-critic基线，多轮且上下文丰富的任务提升更明显。该工作表明信念建模能促进去中心化LLM协作。
papers.abstract_en: Recent work has explored optimizing LLM collaboration through Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL), but many approaches still rely on predefined workflows, limiting efficiency and scalability. Decentralized LLM collaboration is challenging because agents execute independently with limited communication, share a joint objective, and must infer useful information from communication traces. In this paper, we propose BCMAAC, a Belief-Conditioned Multi-Agent Actor-Critic method that maintains beliefs over contextual information and uses them to facilitate training. Experiments on Minecraft game-playing, web searching and tool-using tasks show that BCMAAC improves task performance and collaborative behavior compared to naive actor-critic baselines. The improvements are particularly pronounced in multi-turn tasks with richer contextual information, where belief modeling provides a clear advantage.

papers.title_en: A Unified Arena for LLM Agents across Diverse Eurogame
papers.authors: Fengrui Zhang, Xiang Li, Ruomeng Ding, Jiayi Yuan, Yuchen Huang, Zhaoyang Han, Xiaoliang Wang, Daoyuan Chen, Yaliang Li
papers.evidence: 在竞争性欧式桌游上评测LLM智能体的统一基准竞技场
papers.tldr: 现有LLM智能体评测多局限于单一游戏或执行框架，难以判断竞争优劣势能否跨环境保持。作者提出DECE统一竞技场，覆盖十款欧式桌游并共享接口与评测协议，系统比较9个模型与4种执行框架组成的12种配置。主研究完成480场三人对局，合计1032场，发现跨游戏排名总体一致但存在游戏特异性优势，同一模型换框架表现也会变化。成绩优势未必带来更优token或成本效率，因此应同时按跨游戏竞争表现与资源消耗评估完整智能体配置。
papers.abstract_en: Interactive environments offer a practical way to evaluate large language model (LLM) agents, and competitive games extend this evaluation to decisions shaped by competing goals and other agents' choices. Yet existing evaluations confined to individual games or execution frameworks leave unclear which competitive advantages persist across settings. We introduce DECE (Diverse Eurogame Competitive Environments), a unified arena spanning ten Eurogames with shared interfaces and evaluation protocols. These games combine lasting strategic commitments, competition over shared resources, and multiple routes to victory. Our primary study evaluates 12 model-harness configurations, spanning nine models and four execution harnesses, in 480 three-player matches across ten games. The main and supplementary studies comprise 1,032 completed matches in total. These comparisons reveal broad cross-game ranking agreement alongside game-specific strengths. Matched studies show that the same model can perform differently across execution harnesses, adding another source of variation to these profiles. These performance advantages do not consistently translate into better token or cost efficiency, making resource use an additional consideration when comparing configurations. Together, the findings support evaluating complete agent configurations by both their competitive performance across games and the resources needed to achieve it.

papers.title_en: Reinforcement Learning for the Game of Balatro: A Fast Simulator and Two-Policy Training Approach
papers.authors: Ajay Vikram Periasami, Anjaneya Gupta, Ethan Cheng, Ivan Rosales
papers.evidence: 面向Balatro的快速模拟器与双策略PPO强化学习流程
papers.tldr: Balatro 的动作空间达约3000且依赖状态，回合长达数百步、奖励稀疏，抽牌与商店又高度随机，强化学习难以直接奏效。作者搭建 Rust 高速模拟器并以 BalatroBot 对真实客户端做状态差分校验，提供动态合法动作掩码的紧凑接口，再用双策略 PPO 将战术盲注与战略商店分阶段训练并共享全局状态。联合训练后首盲通关率超过99%，平均回报提升约一个数量级，但平均最高底注仅达3/8；单策略基线在贪心与囤积间震荡。该工作给出强反应式基线，并把剩余差距定位到长程战略规划。
papers.abstract_en: Balatro, a 2024 roguelike deckbuilder, presents three difficulties that have historically derailed reinforcement learning methods: a 3,000-action state-dependent action space, horizons of several hundred decisions with sparse rewards, and pervasive stochasticity in both card draws and shop generation. Published RL results on the game remain scarce. We introduce an end-to-end pipeline comprising (i) a high-throughput Rust simulator that is automatically state-diffed against the live game client via BalatroBot, (ii) a condensed observation-action interface with dynamic per-step masking of legal moves, and (iii) a multi-agent PPO architecture that decomposes play into a tactical blind policy and a strategic shop policy that share the full game state but act in disjoint phases. Long-horizon credit assignment is partially addressed by per-agent reward routing with explicit cross-agent credit. On the main joint run, training metrics show a sharp phase transition in which the first-blind clear rate converges above 99% and mean episode return increases by roughly an order of magnitude, plateauing at a mean maximum ante of 3 out of 8; single-agent baselines under identical rewards oscillated between greedy and hoarding failure modes and did not stably clear the first blind. These results establish the two-policy decomposition as a strong reactive baseline for Balatro and localise the remaining gap to long-horizon strategic planning rather than tactical blind play.

papers.title_en: TaskFrame: Connecting Task-Level Planning with Frame-Level Control for Game Agents
papers.authors: Guangzhi Wang, Junfu Pu, Yiran Wang, Xingyilang Yin, Honghao Chen, Cheng Cheng, Lingen Li, Yinan Zhou, Jiarui Wu, Yinuo Jiang, Hongbo Jin, Xiaodong Cun, Ying Shan
papers.evidence: 视觉语言规划器与帧级控制结合的通用游戏智能体
papers.tldr: 游戏智能体需兼顾高层任务推理与低延迟帧级操控，单一模型难以同时满足两类计算需求。TaskFrame 采用分层规划器-控制器框架，用视觉语言规划器把目标拆成原子指令，并以特殊目标 token 的隐状态作为可缓存目标嵌入。因果 Transformer 控制器结合目标嵌入与近期观测，逐步输出键鼠动作和相机运动，经三阶段训练联合对齐。Minecraft 实验显示其指令分解具竞争力，闭环战斗成功率高于基线。
papers.abstract_en: Building general game agents requires both high-level task reasoning and low-latency action control in rapidly changing visual environments. These capabilities favor models with substantially different computational profiles, making them difficult to realize within a single model. In this work, we present TaskFrame, a hierarchical planner-controller framework that connects task-level planning with frame-level keyboard-and-mouse control. A vision-language task planner decomposes a high-level goal into an ordered sequence of atomic instructions and is optimized through supervised learning and dependency-aware GRPO. The hidden states of special goal tokens that terminate each atomic instruction provide continuous goal embeddings that are cached and reused across control steps. A causal Transformer controller combines the embedding of the active goal with recent observations to predict discrete keyboard and mouse-button actions and continuous camera motion at every game step. We train the system in three stages: planner training, controller pretraining, and joint alignment. Experiments in Minecraft show that TaskFrame is competitive with general-purpose vision-language models on instruction decomposition, and that in closed-loop evaluation the agent achieves a higher combat success rate than the evaluated baselines.

papers.title_en: Rome Wasn't Built in One Turn: Replay-Grounded Reward Signals for Long-Horizon Freeciv Agents
papers.authors: Yanchen Liu, Xinyu Che, Brihi Joshi, Renzo Fukuda, Junhua Liu, Ruifeng Li, Yunfei Ge, Hang Yan, Xiang Ren
papers.evidence: 面向长程策略游戏语言模型智能体的回放式奖励信号
papers.tldr: 长程策略游戏奖励稀疏，局内分数常与最终结果背离，论文称“记分牌陷阱”。作者构建CivHarness，可保存状态、分支决策并回放未来，训练LLM裁判CivTelescope比较两个局面优劣。再用其作密集奖励训练Freeciv智能体CivMarshmallow，在中局获得8.94分阶段增益，比最佳基线高77%。该工作以回放验证的奖励信号缓解长程反馈稀疏问题。
papers.abstract_en: Training language-model agents to play long-horizon strategy games is hard because deterministic feedback is sparse and often arrives only at the end of a game. In-game scores can offer dense signals, but they do not reliably predict future outcomes: in 8-68% of position pairs across eight strategy games, the higher-scoring position leads to the worse outcome. We term this phenomenon scoreboard traps. In Freeciv, an open-source turn-based empire-building game where several players manage units, cities, and diplomacy over hundreds of turns, we look into better reward signals for gameplay agents. To facilitate this, we build CivHarness, an open system that saves current game states, branches on different decisions, and replays the game to future turns to provide measurable long-horizon feedback from saved positions. We use CivHarness to train CivTelescope, an LLM Judge that predicts which one of two game positions will yield the better outcome. On scoreboard-trap pairs, CivTelescope is 1.3-2.0 times more accurate than off-the-shelf language models, and it generalizes to new game starts, later turns, and unseen rules. We then train a Freeciv gameplay agent with CivTelescope as a dense reward, and call this recipe CivMarshmallow. When used in the middle stage of the game where scoreboard traps are common, CivMarshmallow reaches an average training phase gain of 8.94 points, 77% more than the best baseline, the end-of-game reward. Over the full 120-turn game, CivMarshmallow uses a hybrid reward that starts from the scoreboard or the end-of-game reward and shifts to CivTelescope as the game advances; this hybrid reward scores highest among the rewards we compare.

papers.title_en: EvolveMAS: A Unified Self-Evolution Framework for Decentralized Multi-Agent Systems
papers.authors: Yalun Wu, Qiwei Ma, Bingbing Xu, Dan Zhang, Long Bai, Boyang Wang, Jiatong Li, Zheqi Lv, Shaozu Yuan, Peiying Wang, Jiawei Wang, An Zhang, Tat-Seng Chua
papers.evidence: 面向去中心化大模型多智能体系统的自进化框架
papers.tldr: 去中心化多智能体系统需在测试时适应同伴并复用经验，但现有方法多针对单一交互设定。EvolveMAS为主智能体配备MemoryAgent，在推理上下文外维护结构化记忆，并联合回合内在线适应与跨回合知识演化。在覆盖合作、混合动机和对抗设定的五个基准、六种配置上，其归一化平均分达77.2，优于对比方法。消融与交互轨迹表明测试时记忆治理和跨回合知识复用均有效，为无参数更新的经验驱动适应提供统一框架。
papers.abstract_en: Decentralized multi-agent systems (MAS) enable large language model agents to interact without centralized control. Agents need to adapt to other agents at test time and reuse accumulated experience to refine their interaction strategies for future interactions across cooperative, mixed-motive, and adversarial settings. However, existing approaches often develop adaptation mechanisms for particular interaction settings. This raises a central question: how can decentralized MAS support test-time adaptation and reliable experience reuse across interaction settings? We propose EvolveMAS, a unified self-evolution framework that supports experience-driven adaptation within and across episodes. EvolveMAS pairs each main agent with a dedicated MemoryAgent for test-time memory governance, which maintains isolated Structured Memory outside the main agent's reasoning context. EvolveMAS organizes adaptation into two complementary processes: Within-Episode Online Adaptation and Cross-Episode Knowledge Evolution. During Within-Episode Online Adaptation, MemoryAgent updates episodic, semantic, and working memory from interaction evidence to inform subsequent actions. During Cross-Episode Knowledge Evolution, the main agent uses memory and episode outcomes to distill reusable interaction knowledge comprising partner profiles and interaction strategies for subsequent episodes. Across five benchmarks and six evaluation configurations spanning the three interaction settings, EvolveMAS achieves the highest normalized average score of 77.2 among the compared methods. Ablations show that test-time memory governance and cross-episode knowledge reuse both improve performance. Interaction traces further illustrate how updated memory and distilled knowledge guide subsequent interactions. These results support experience-driven adaptation in decentralized MAS without updating model parameters.

papers.title_en: Preference-Guided Cooperation in Multi-Objective Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
papers.evidence: 面向多智能体合作的目标级反事实信用分配
papers.tldr: 多目标多智能体强化学习需同时处理智能体协调与目标权衡，但现有方法常把合作和多目标优化分开建模，复杂度高。本文提出MIRL，引入目标级反事实信用分配评估智能体对各目标的贡献，并利用元梯度让智能体个体学习目标优先级，同时协同优化系统级目标，包含静态MIRL-S和动态MIRL-D。在多目标粒子环境实验中，方法提升Pareto前沿质量，动态版本表现最佳，说明多目标结构本身可有效引导合作。
papers.abstract_en: Multi-objective multi-agent reinforcement learning (MOMARL) addresses agent coordination and objective trade-offs simultaneously while optimising overall system performance. Existing work tends to treat multi-agent cooperation and multi-objective optimisation as largely independent components of a learning problem, which amounts to an exorbitant complexity except in trivial cases. We study here whether the structure provided by multiple objectives can itself be exploited to facilitate cooperation, rather than being treated as an additional optimisation challenge. We formulate MOMARL at both the team and individual levels and introduce objective-wise counterfactual credit assignment to evaluate each agent's contribution across the team objectives. We propose Meta-Gradient Informed Multi-Objective Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MIRL), with static (MIRL-S) and dynamic (MIRL-D) variants. By incorporating meta-gradient information, MIRL enables agents to learn how to prioritise objectives individually while collectively optimising the system-level objective, allowing the multi-objective structure to directly guide cooperation. Experiments on a multi-objective multiple particle environment show that our methods improve Pareto-front quality over baselines, with the dynamic variant achieving the strongest performance.

papers.title_en: FOCUS: Active Critic Learning for Long-Horizon Language Model Agents
papers.authors: Zhengping Jiang, William Jurayj, Liaoyaqi Wang, Chunsheng Zuo, Anqi Liu, Benjamin Van Durme
papers.evidence: 面向长程语言模型智能体的主动评论家学习与TD优势信用分配
papers.tldr: 长程语言模型智能体因稀疏结果奖励难以对早期动作做信用分配，学习式critic又可能估值不准，而重复续写采样成本高昂。FOCUS用选择性分支让rollout控制器优先从预期最能降低critic误差的状态采样续写，并以TD(λ)优势为状态间片段打分、用采样证据训练critic。其模块化上下文管理接口将上下文管理与rollout分配解耦。在匹配每步生成预算下，FOCUS于法律推理、深度搜索和代码定位任务上优于GRPO与VinePPO，Qwen3.5-9B上BrowseComp-Plus提升7.2分、DeonticBench提升4.1分。
papers.abstract_en: Sparse outcome rewards make it difficult for long-horizon language-model agents to assign credit to earlier actions. Learned critics provide value estimates for intermediate states, but these estimates can be inaccurate, while estimating intermediate values with repetitive continuation samples from points within a trajectory incurs substantial costs. To mitigate these issues, we introduce FOCUS, an RL method that uses selective branching to help the critic network learn its value estimator. The rollout controller facilitates active learning for the critic by sampling continuations from states that are expected to most reduce the critic's estimation error. These refined value estimates then score the segment between consecutive states with a TD($λ$) advantage, while the sampled evidence supplies training targets for the critic. FOCUS supports long-horizon agentic reinforcement learning through a modular context-management interface that decouples context management from rollout allocation. Our experiments show that using compaction-induced segment boundaries for value estimation and credit assignment, FOCUS outperforms GRPO and VinePPO with matched per-step generation budgets on legal reasoning, deep search, and code localization benchmarks, improving held-out accuracy at Qwen3.5-9B scale by 7.2 points over the strongest baseline on BrowseComp-Plus (55.4 vs. 48.2) and by 4.1 points on DeonticBench (56.5 vs. 52.4).

papers.title_en: Vision-Language Agents Can Learn in Their Own Latent Worlds
papers.authors: Haoxi Li, Sikai Bai, Jianfei Ma, Qinglin Hou, Xiaocheng Lu, Tao Han, Jie Zhang, Song Guo
papers.evidence: 将视觉语言模型重构为潜在世界模型的基于模型强化学习
papers.tldr: 预训练视觉语言模型蕴含丰富世界知识，却难以通过在线交互持续提升策略；且策略更新会改变交互分布，频繁更新大模型代价高。Dwell将VLM重构为循环潜在转移算子，使其在潜在空间中预测、调整与行动，并同时充当世界模型与策略。它在五个交互视觉环境中取得可训练方法里最强整体表现，并显著降低想象计算量。结果表明，面向动作的未来预测比重建未来更关键。
papers.abstract_en: Learning from experience is essential for building the next generation of agents that continually expand their capabilities. Pretrained vision-language models (VLMs) already internalize rich world knowledge, yet this knowledge is rarely leveraged to drive policy improvement through online interaction. Realizing this potential efficiently remains challenging, as policy updates shift the agent's interaction distribution, requiring the world model to adapt accordingly, while continually updating large pretrained models is computationally expensive. To address this challenge, we introduce Dwell, a model-based reinforcement learning (RL) framework that reframes a VLM as a recurrent latent transition operator, endowing it with the ability to predict, adjust, and act in latent space. Leveraging the VLM's own representations and its dual role as both world model and policy, the agent continually learns from real interactions to anticipate and evaluate action outcomes, and from latent imagination to improve its behavior. Across five interactive visual environments, Dwell achieves the strongest overall performance among trainable methods while substantially reducing the compute required for imagination, showing that effective world models for VLM agents need not reconstruct the future; they need to predict futures that are useful for action. Our code is publicly available at https://github.com/Tom111-lhx/Dwell

papers.title_en: Action-Value Calibration via Continuation Sharing for Long-Horizon Agentic Reinforcement Learning
papers.authors: Yingjian Chen, Lang Zhou, Zixin Zhao, Pingfan Li, Weishi Zheng, Zhilin Zhao
papers.evidence: 面向长程智能体强化学习的信用分配与动作价值校准
papers.tldr: 长程智能体强化学习依赖交互序列反馈，个体动作的信用分配困难；GiGPO等共享状态比较仍只用单条采样延续估计动作价值，易受后续决策影响。ConCal利用同一回合批次中已有延续证据，按进入状态-动作-状态转移匹配同一任务访问，融合共享延续证据与各自转移估计，并反向传播校准值以修正早期动作价值。在ALFWorld和WebShop上，基于Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct，成功率分别较GiGPO提升3.39和5.86个百分点。该方法无需额外采样即可降低对单条延续的依赖，缓解局部信用扭曲。
papers.abstract_en: Reinforcement learning for long-horizon agents relies on feedback from sequences of interactions, making credit assignment to individual actions difficult. Existing methods such as GiGPO compare actions at shared states to compute relative advantages, but estimate each action's value from a single sampled continuation. The resulting local credit remains sensitive to decisions made later in the trajectory. To address this problem, we propose ConCal (Continuation Calibration), a recursive continuation-value estimator that incorporates continuation evidence already present in a rollout batch. ConCal matches visits from the same task by their incoming state-action-state transitions, combines shared continuation evidence with each visit's own transition estimate, and propagates calibrated values backward to refine earlier action-value estimates. This reduces dependence on individual sampled continuations and mitigates local credit distortions without additional rollouts. Held-out return diagnostics show lower error in within-group value differences and higher agreement with reference action orderings than estimates based on individual continuations. With Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct, ConCal improves success rates over GiGPO by 3.39 and 5.86 percentage points on ALFWorld and WebShop, respectively. Our code is available at https://github.com/Yingjian-Chen/ConCal.

papers.title_en: MRC-MMAgent: Reinforcement Learning for Multi-Role Collaboration in Multimodal Tool-Using Agents
papers.authors: Shengqin Wang, Jie Jin, Xiaofan Li, Wentao Yan, Yu Cheng, Qingsong HuYihang Chen, Weilin Luo, Jingyu Gong, Xin Tan, Yuan Xie, Zhizhong Zhang
papers.evidence: 面向多模态工具使用大模型智能体的多角色协同强化学习
papers.tldr: 多模态工具使用智能体需借助外部工具解决复杂任务，但现有强化学习多只训练单一角色并以终局奖励优化，忽略检索中的检查、改写与修正过程。MRC-MMAgent 将求解、检查与继续求解组成多角色协作循环，把轨迹评估和续解直接嵌入可执行智能体回路。它还用角色耦合目标联合优化任务成功、交互有效性与成功修正，并做全轨迹策略学习。仅用原始基线训练集，该方法在多个基准上稳定优于对应基座模型，取得领先或极具竞争力的表现。
papers.abstract_en: Multimodal tool-using agents augment vision-language models with access to external information and capabilities, enabling them to solve knowledge-intensive and visually complex tasks that cannot be addressed using visual context alone. However, existing reinforcement learning pipelines largely train single-role agents to search and answer using terminal rewards, overlooking how humans inspect retrieved evidence, reformulate queries, and revise conclusions during search. Consequently, they fail to optimize this self-corrective process over complete interaction trajectories. We propose MRC-MMAgent, a multi-role collaborative reinforcement learning framework that incorporates trajectory assessment and continuation directly into the executable agent loop. First, the framework establishes a multi-role collaborative loop that integrates solving, inspection, and continuation, enabling the agent to acquire evidence through tools, evaluate the preceding trajectory, and resume problem solving when the current answer is insufficiently supported. Second, we introduce a role-coupled learning objective that combines task success, interaction validity, and successful correction with full-trajectory policy optimization across the decisions generated by all roles. Extensive experiments show that, using only the original baseline training set without constructing additional datasets, our method consistently outperforms the corresponding base models and achieves leading or highly competitive performance across benchmarks.

papers.title_en: EnvLunch: The Environment as a Free Lunch for Learning to Interact
papers.authors: Wei Liu, Min Gao, Yali Du, Yulan He
papers.evidence: 利用环境产生的可验证任务为智能体强化学习预热
papers.tldr: 针对智能体数据分析依赖大量人工标注任务的问题，EnvLunch利用可执行数据库环境本身提供的交互结构与可验证结果，构造无需标注的预热训练。方法采样有效动作轨迹并执行得到最终观测，再让智能体仅凭最终观测恢复功能等价轨迹。该无标签预热在多种下游训练预算下平均超过基线9分以上，少标签时基线需8至32倍标注样本才能匹配其最小预算精度。它还优于让模型自写任务，并可迁移到数据分析之外的微调。
papers.abstract_en: For agentic data analysis, language-model agents often require a large number of annotated tasks to learn how to interact effectively with executable environments (i.e., databases). While high-quality annotated tasks require heavy manual effort, an executable environment already provides rich interaction structure and verifiable outcomes. In this sense, the environment itself offers a free lunch, an additional set of verifiable tasks that require no human annotation. We propose EnvLunch, a warm-up stage that turns this environmental signal into agent training without human-written or model-generated task descriptions, before downstream agentic reinforcement learning. EnvLunch samples valid action trajectories, executes them to obtain final observations, and trains an agent to recover a functionally equivalent trajectory given only its final observation. This label-free warm-up enables the model to outperform the baseline by over 9 points on average across all downstream training budgets, and with few labels, the baseline needs 8 to 32 times as many annotated examples to match the accuracy that the EnvLunch model reaches at its smallest training budget. Letting the environment alone define the task yields a larger gain than having the model write its own tasks over the same environments, and this warm-up also improves fine-tuning on benchmarks beyond data analysis. EnvLunch therefore saves annotated tasks and provides a better starting point for fine-tuning agentic models when such tasks are limited.

papers.title_en: Self-Evolution Reasoner: Continuous Optimization via Policy-Intrinsic Exploration and Exploitation
papers.authors: Wenhang Shi, Yiren Chen, Zhe Zhao, Jinhao Dong, Wei Lu, Xiaoyong Du
papers.evidence: 面向大模型自我改进的内在探索策略优化
papers.tldr: RLVR与自监督同策略蒸馏均受探索瓶颈限制，策略难采样有效解而陷入局部最优，外部示范又因离策略和分布不匹配妨碍自我进化。SEPO用标签引导策略产生正确推理以增强探索，再以同分布推理为条件让当前策略充当自教师，将新解蒸馏回策略，迭代实现策略内在的探索与利用。在科学、工具使用和复杂逻辑推理中，同等训练时间或步数下SEPO性能最佳，效率与收敛上限更高。复杂任务和小模型等基线失败场景仍稳定提升，表明持续自我进化可行。
papers.abstract_en: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) enables large language models (LLMs) to continuously self-improve their reasoning capabilities. Compared to RLVR's scalar rewards, recent self-supervised on-policy distillation methods leverage denser supervision signals. However, both paradigms suffer from exploration bottlenecks, struggling to escape local optima when the policy fails to sample valid solutions. Relying on external demonstrations can bypass this issue; however, the off-policy nature hinders genuine self-improvement and the mismatched-distribution reasoning can not be fully exploited. In this work, we propose Self-Evolution Policy Optimization (SEPO), a framework that drives continuous reasoning capability evolution via guided exploration and in-distribution exploitation. Specifically, SEPO utilizes labels to elicit correct reasoning from the policy, unlocking the exploration potential. By treating current policy conditioned on this in-distribution reasoning as a self-teacher, SEPO distills the newly discovered solution back into the policy. Through this iterative cycle of policy-intrinsic exploration and exploitation, SEPO achieves robust and continuous capability evolution. Across scientific, tool-use, and complex logical reasoning domains, SEPO consistently achieves the best performance under identical training time or steps, demonstrating superior efficiency and convergence ceilings. Notably, SEPO maintains stable improvements even in scenarios where baselines severely underperform or fail entirely, such as on complex tasks or with small-scale models. Our code is available at https://github.com/Eric8932/SEPO.

papers.title_en: How Humans Learn Unfamiliar Worlds: A Think-Aloud Dataset on ARC-AGI-3
papers.authors: Shuzhi Liu, Archana Warrier, Dat Nguyen, Chengqi Zheng, Kevin Ellis, Yewen Pu
papers.evidence: 比较人类与大模型智能体探索新游戏环境的出声思维数据集
papers.tldr: 理解通用智能需追踪学习者如何在交互中构建与修正世界模型，但缺少细粒度人类探索数据。作者以ARC-AGI-3为测试平台，采集64名参与者25款游戏的144条轨迹，同步记录动作与出声思维，并补充250条LLM智能体轨迹及机制触发、动作意图、错误恢复标注。分析发现人类更常用定性表征且常无明确假设地探索，成功人类轨迹中定性表征占50.0%，成功LLM仅14.3%。该数据集将认知过程与观察动作对齐，为诊断LLM和设计下一代基准提供依据。
papers.abstract_en: Learning through exploration and using newly acquired knowledge to achieve goals are central capabilities of general intelligence. Understanding these capabilities requires tracing how learners build, use, and revise world models during interaction. We construct the first dataset that records how humans discover and use the mechanisms of novel environments, using ARC-AGI-3 as a testbed: 144 trajectories from 64 participants across 25 public games, each pairing time-synchronized actions with think-aloud audio, plus 250 trajectories from large language model (LLM) agents with and without harnesses on the same games. We annotate mechanism triggers and recognition, action purposes, and errors and recovery, linking changes in understanding to the observations and actions that support them. We analyze characteristics of human cognition and compare them with those of LLM agents. Both groups anticipate mechanisms and use familiar analogies. Qualitative representations are more common in successful human trajectories than in successful LLM trajectories (50.0% versus 14.3%). Humans more often explore unfamiliar situations without a concrete hypothesis, while hypothesis testing is common in both groups. We also trace how learners recover through belief revision, replanning, and execution correction. As LLMs with well-designed harnesses reach saturated performance on public ARC-AGI-3 games, our cognitive analyses motivate next-generation benchmarks that challenge familiar priors, require accumulated evidence and abstraction, and test planning through subgoals, experimentation, and recovery. Our dataset is available at [https://arc3-human-think-aloud.github.io/](https://arc3-human-think-aloud.github.io/).

papers.title_en: DTCA: Denoising Token Credit Assignment for Reinforcement Learning in Diffusion Language Models
papers.authors: Hongze Chen, Miao Pan, Lizhou Liang, Qinfeng Li, Xinyin Ma, Yongliang Shen, Weishi Wang, Daniel Dahlmeier, Xuhong Zhang, Wenqi Zhang
papers.evidence: 面向语言模型强化学习的词元级信用分配
papers.tldr: 扩散语言模型通过迭代去噪生成文本，但最终结果奖励难以说明各 token 的贡献，使强化学习信用分配困难。DTCA 利用 token 提交后剩余掩码位置预测置信度的提升来估计 token 贡献，按词性分组，并据此选择去噪时间步、分配 token 级学习信号，还用策略更新引起的熵变进行校准。在 LLaDA-8B-Instruct 上，该方法在不同生成预算下稳定提升数学推理，MATH500 最高提升 9.0 分，GSM8K 提升 5.3 分。
papers.abstract_en: Diffusion language models (DLMs) generate text through iterative denoising, enabling bidirectional context modeling and parallel token refinement. Recent studies have applied reinforcement learning (RL) to DLMs and improved their reasoning performance. However, the iterative denoising process makes credit assignment more challenging, as final outcome rewards provide limited information about how different tokens contribute to the final output. In this paper, we propose Denoising Token Credit Assignment (DTCA), a framework for token-level credit assignment in reinforcement learning for diffusion language models. DTCA estimates token contributions by measuring the improvement in prediction confidence of remaining masked positions after token commitment and groups these signals according to part-of-speech (POS) categories. These contribution weights are used to select informative denoising timesteps and assign token-level learning signals during RL training. DTCA further calibrates these learning signals according to token-level entropy changes induced by policy updates. Experiments on LLaDA-8B-Instruct show that DTCA consistently improves mathematical reasoning performance across different generation budgets, with gains of up to 9.0 points on MATH500 and 5.3 points on GSM8K over the base model.

papers.title_en: Human-Feedback-Guided Multi-Agent Inverse Reinforcement Learning for Interactive Driving Behavior Modeling
papers.authors: Longhao Yan, Jinhao Liang, Kaidi Yang
papers.evidence: 面向交互驾驶行为的多智能体逆强化学习
papers.tldr: 驾驶行为建模对混合交通下自动驾驶决策至关重要，但现有奖励学习多为单智能体且忽略人类反馈。本文提出HFG-MAIRL，将每辆车与直接交互邻居建模为局部马尔可夫博弈，并用聚合交通状态表征环境，通过有限边缘响应迭代近似耦合多车响应。方法还以Bradley-Terry似然将人类序数偏好作为监督，实验用驾驶员情绪标签构建成对偏好约束。在AIDE数据集上，该框架在决策建模上优于代表性IRL基线，并产生可解释且与反馈对齐的奖励模式。
papers.abstract_en: Modeling human driving behavior is fundamental to understanding driver decision-making and supporting autonomous vehicles (AVs) in mixed traffic. Reward learning offers a principled way to infer the latent objectives behind driving behaviors, yet most existing methods are formulated in single-agent settings and treat surrounding vehicles as dynamic obstacles. Directly extending reward learning to multi-agent scenarios is difficult because the joint action space grows exponentially with the number of interacting vehicles. In addition, existing approaches mainly rely on physical demonstrations and rarely exploit human feedback during reward recovery. To address these limitations, this paper proposes a Human-Feedback-Guided Multi-Agent Inverse Reinforcement Learning (HFG-MAIRL) framework for interactive driving behavior modeling. First, we develop a multi-agent maximum-entropy inverse reinforcement learning module that explicitly models each vehicle and its directly interacting neighbors in a localized Markov game, while using aggregated traffic states to capture the influence of the broader traffic environment. The resulting coupled multi-vehicle responses are approximated through finite marginal-response iterations over factorized vehicle-level policies, avoiding explicit enumeration of the full joint action space. Second, we incorporate human feedback as ordinal preference supervision through a Bradley-Terry likelihood. In our experiments, driver emotion labels are used as one instantiation of such feedback and converted into pairwise ordinal preference constraints. Experiments on the AIDE dataset show that HFG-MAIRL outperforms representative IRL baselines in decision modeling and produces interpretable feedback-aligned reward patterns.

papers.title_en: CORMA: Constraint-Routed Decision Mamba for Generalizable Multi-Constraint Offline Safe Reinforcement Learning
papers.authors: Changxu Ni, Feiran You, Yongan Guo, Hongyang Du, Kang Wei, Le Liang, Yiyang Ni, Jun Li
papers.evidence: 可泛化的多约束离线安全强化学习
papers.tldr: 离线安全强化学习需在满足约束下从静态数据学习策略，但现有Decision Transformer方法多面向单约束，难以泛化到未见多安全预算组合且计算开销高。CORMA将策略推断分解为约束感知RTG估计与自适应动作生成，用约束专家和路由引导的专家乘积融合，并为Mamba动作解码器提供安全引导。在OSRL基准上，它取得更优奖励-安全权衡，推理延迟较DT方法降低37%，对未见安全预算组合的零样本泛化更强。
papers.abstract_en: Offline safe reinforcement learning (RL) learns safety-aware policies from static datasets while satisfying safety constraints during deployment. Motivated by the strong trajectorymodeling capabilities of Transformers, recent Decision Transformer (DT)-based methods formulate offline safe RL as conditional sequence modeling by conditioning action generation on return-to-go (RTG) and cost-to-go (CTG) tokens, thereby enabling adaptation to varying safety budgets. However, existing DT-based methods are developed for single-constraint tasks. For tasks with multiple constraints, generalizing learned policies to unseen combinations of safety budgets remains challenging due to the conflicting requirements imposed by heterogeneous constraints. Moreover, the quadratic complexity of Transformer architectures significantly increases the computational overhead in multi-constraint tasks, as representing additional constraints requires more CTG tokens. Recently, Mamba has emerged as an efficient sequence-modeling backbone, offering linear computational complexity and strong generalization capabilities. In this paper, we propose CORMA, a constraint-routed decision Mamba framework for generalizable multi-constraint offline safe RL. CORMA decomposes policy inference into constraint-aware RTG estimation and adaptive action generation, where constraint-specific experts model feasible RTG distributions and a router-guided product-of-experts mechanism fuses these distributions to provide safety-aware guidance for a Mamba-based action decoder. A three-stage optimization strategy is designed to improve training stability. Extensive experiments on OSRL benchmarks demonstrate that CORMA achieves superior reward-safety trade-offs, reduces inference latency by 37% compared with DT-based methods, and exhibits stronger zero-shot generalization to unseen safety-budget combinations than offline safe RL baselines.

papers.title_en: MultiEvoSkill: Structure-Aware Multi-Agent Skill Evolution for Generalizable Skill Artifacts
papers.authors: Kounianhua Du, Jianxing Liu, Ruoshui Shan, Yucheng Zhang, Ke Li, Xing Sun, Weinan Zhang
papers.evidence: 面向大模型智能体的结构感知多智能体技能演化
papers.tldr: 冻结LLM智能体依赖技能文档适配，但现有技能生成受人类或单模型视角限制，且难以表达并行分支与依赖。MultiEvoSkill将技能编译为类型图，结合异构多智能体集体修订与结构感知辩论演化，在依赖和重要性约束下蒸馏编辑，并用多维门控保证信息增益与拓扑正确。实验与消融表明其优于SOTA并提升跨模型泛化，为图结构化技能演化提供新框架。
papers.abstract_en: Skill documents are becoming the default adaptation surface for frozen large language model (LLM) agents, but current skill generators face two key limitations. First, humans and different LLMs differ in how they organize procedural knowledge and approach task solving. Skills authored from a human or single-model perspective may therefore fail to align with the reasoning behaviors of other backbones, limiting cross-model generalization. Second, sequential skill descriptions inadequately represent procedures with parallel branches and explicit dependencies, while existing skill optimizers primarily operate on prose and lack explicit support for graph-structured skill evolution. We introduce MultiEvoSkill, a skill-optimization framework comprising three core components: 1) Skill compiler casts the skill as a typed graph with tailored operators, producing a compact, informative representation with explicit procedural topology; 2) Heterogeneous agent system proposes revision advices using collective intelligence, where minimal and informative issues are identified based on multiple sets of experiences. 3) Structure-aware debate and evolution mechanism organizes candidate edits into a heterogeneous graph, resolves them under dependency and importance constraints, and distills the collective proposal into the artifact. Multi-dimensional gating ensures the information gain and topological correctness of each evolution. Optimal skills are then obtained when the system converges at a consistent state. Various experiments and ablations against SOTA methods validate the effectiveness and generalization of MultiEvoSkill.

papers.title_en: IntNet: A Communication-Driven Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning Framework for Cooperative Autonomous Driving
papers.authors: Leandro Parada, Kevin Yu, Panagiotis Angeloudis
papers.evidence: 面向协同自动驾驶的多智能体强化学习框架
papers.tldr: 多智能体强化学习用于自动驾驶面临非平稳、部分可观测与协同安全难题，仅共享编码观测不足以应对安全关键场景。IntNet将车辆意图传输与自适应通信调度统一到端到端学习框架，用观测预测模块预判后续策略输出，并通过图注意力网络处理消息、调度器优化通信图。在城市复杂交通中，它提升协同并降低碰撞率，通信开销最多减少60%。该工作表明意图级通信与带宽感知调度可兼顾安全与效率。
papers.abstract_en: Achieving safety in autonomous driving through Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) is a critical yet challenging task due to non-stationarity, partial observability, and the need for effective coordination among agents. Although earlier cooperative MARL methods have aimed to improve coordination by sharing encoded state observations, we find these strategies are insufficient in safety-critical scenarios. To address this gap, we present IntNet, a novel MARL framework that enhances safety by incorporating the transmission of vehicle intent and adaptive communication scheduling into a unified end-to-end learning paradigm, jointly optimising all components for safe coordination. Central to our approach is an observation prediction module that enables agents to forecast subsequent policy outputs, which they can then share across a vehicle-to-vehicle network. Our model-free architecture employs a Graph Attention Network to process incoming messages and a scheduler component to dynamically optimise the communication graph for bandwidth efficiency. We compare IntNet against state-of-the-art communicative MARL methods in complex urban environments with both autonomous and human-operated vehicles, achieving improved coordination, lower collision rates, and reducing communication efforts by up to 60\%. Through extensive experiments, we assess the framework's learning efficiency, scalability, and the balance between information sharing and bandwidth usage for collision-free trajectories.
